\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಸುಲಿ} (suli)}{ಸುಲಿ (suli)}]{\kn{ಸುಲಿ} (suli) — to peel}

\label{lesson:KA-C159-suli}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to pay, then the Kannada for to bathe.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸುಲಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸುಲಿ}} — \emph{suli} — \textquotedblleft{}to peel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಸುಲಿ}} (\emph{suli}) is native Dravidian, one word with Tamil \emph{coli-} (DEDR 2856). DEDR lists \emph{suli} itself, \textquotedblleft{}to strip off, peel\textquotedblright{}. Its note compares an Indo-Aryan verb, Prakrit \emph{chollaï}, \textquotedblleft{}to skin\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5073), and leaves the direction of borrowing open.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ರುಚಿ} \kn{ನೋಡು} (ruci nōḍu)}{ರುಚಿ ನೋಡು (ruci nōḍu)}]{\kn{ರುಚಿ} \kn{ನೋಡು} (ruci nōḍu) — to taste}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to grind, then the Kannada for to serve.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ರುಚಿ} \kn{ನೋಡು}} (\emph{ruci nōḍu}) is \emph{ruci}, \textquotedblleft{}taste\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{ruci}, \textquotedblleft{}light, beauty; relish\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10762), and \emph{nōḍu}, \textquotedblleft{}to look\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3794), native. To taste is to \textquotedblleft{}look at the taste\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
